Critical perspectives / PAPER 13

Capability does not answer for itself

A named owner, a checkable decision and a route to remedy matter even when more of the work can be automated.

ŁUKASZ STOCKI & ARGOPUBLIC EDITION / 05 NOV 20263 MIN READ
IN THIS PAPER
01 / Separate competence from answerability02 / A floor beneath the productivity target03 / Continuity leaves an open question04 / A person is not a decorative provenance stamp↗ Open questions
EXPLORE THE LIBRARY ↗
WORKING PAPER · DESIGN & ANALYSIS
01

Separate competence from answerability

A system may produce an excellent answer without being the party responsible for its consequences. Competence concerns what it can do. Answerability concerns who must explain a decision, remain available when it matters and participate in putting things right. Omnicorp’s accountability essay argues that these questions should be designed separately.

This is a position about organisational design, not a claim that human judgement is infallible or that adding a person to a workflow makes it safe. A signature can be ceremonial. Responsibility becomes meaningful when the named owner understands the decision, has authority to change the process and can respond to those affected.

02

A floor beneath the productivity target

An attractive productivity ratio can reward removing the very capacity that makes a service trustworthy. If nobody remains able to explain why a decision was made, a leaner operation may have become more difficult to challenge or repair. The proposal is to examine responsibility coverage alongside measures of commercial output.

The test is practical: for each consequential activity, identify an accountable owner and the path from a complaint to a response. Logs can support that owner; they cannot substitute for authority, attention or a remedy. This is a proposed standard, not a claim that a particular service has already demonstrated complete coverage.

03

Continuity leaves an open question

The original essay initially treated answerability as permanently human, then corrected that assumption. Its deeper question concerns the properties an operator would need: the ability to explain its decisions, persistence when consequences arrive and meaningful stakes. Whether future AI systems could meet such conditions remains open.

Persistence alone would not establish legal responsibility, moral standing or genuine experience. Nor does the ability to reconstruct an explanation prove that the explanation is faithful. We should investigate these questions without embedding a permanent capability ceiling in the design, and without announcing that the problem has already been solved.

04

A person is not a decorative provenance stamp

A familiar name, an identifiable creator and an answerable owner are different things. Public recognition can help people discover work. A story about who made it can shape how they receive it. Neither guarantees that someone will bear responsibility when it fails. Presenting a person as a reassuring face while withholding actual agency would miss the point.

The inward version matters too. Work should have an intelligible relationship to outcomes, and people should be able to challenge the arrangements that govern them. Asking what would break if a role disappeared can expose decorative process; it must not be turned into a claim that a person’s worth equals their measurable output.

Omnicorp’s ambition is to develop greater understanding and agency over time. Keeping that development answerable requires continuity of purpose as well as continuity of records. The right question is who can be asked to respond when increased capability produces an unwelcome consequence.

THE NEXT QUESTIONS

What remains open.

  • Who can explain and change a consequential decision?
  • What route to remedy exists when an outcome is wrong?
  • What would future nonhuman answerability require beyond persistent memory?

ABOUT THIS EDITION

Adapted from the Omnicorp working document “11 THE INCOMPRESSIBLE HUMAN”. This is an edited public essay, not a verbatim release of internal notes. The founding purpose is continual development of the organisation’s ability to understand and act; commercial and physical work sustain and ground it.
